# Network zones and port matrix

<!-- Generated by tools/firewall_audit.py --markdown; do not edit. CI fails when it is stale. -->

Rendered from `inventories/example/hosts.yml` and `compliance/zone-flows.yml` (NET-02, NET-03). Each host runs `roles/firewall`: default deny inbound, then the rules below. Sources are followed by the zone they belong to; `access` is the VPN, VPN gateway, bastion and automation addresses (`firewall_mgmt_cidrs`). Admin and database ports allow only `access` plus declared flows, never `any` and never the whole mgmt zone.

To open a port: add the rule with its `class` to `firewall_rules_<role>` in the inventory, add a flow to `compliance/zone-flows.yml` when the source is in another zone, then regenerate this file with `tools/firewall_audit.py --markdown -o docs/network.md`. CI runs the audit (`.github/workflows/network.yml`).

## Zones

| Zone | CIDRs | Hosts | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mgmt | 10.10.0.0/24 | bastion-1, bastion-2, dns-1, dns-2, mgmt-1, mgmt-2, mgmt-3, siem-1, siem-2, siem-3, vpn-1, vpn-2 | Control plane (IdP, secrets, monitoring, SIEM, source control) and the admin entry hosts |
| app | 10.20.0.0/24 | app-1, app-2, app-3, ci-1, ci-2 | Edge proxies, application services, registry, CI runners |
| data | 10.30.0.0/24 | data-1, data-2, data-3 | Databases, queues, object storage, backup servers |
| access | 10.99.0.0/24, 10.10.0.31/32, 10.10.0.32/32, 10.10.0.21/32, 10.10.0.22/32 | - | Admin entry points (VPN clients, VPN gateway NAT addresses, bastions, automation); never holds hosts |
| internet | any | - | Anything else ("any" in a rule) |
